methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Problem and Solution
content: Problem: Students tend to mix up the verbs "do" and "make", and often fail to produce their irregular past tense forms ("did" and "made") accurately.

Solution: Group "task" verbs (do, make, have, take) together within a highly relatable context (daily chores and routines). By anchoring these verbs to specific, frequent collocations (did homework, made the bed, took a shower), students memorize the verb phrases as single cognitive chunks.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Teacher pull-out rotation during independent time:
S1: vocabulary drill — teacher says Vietnamese/mime, student says English + makes sentence.
S2: grammar pattern practice — teacher asks "What did you do yesterday?" → student answers using past task verbs.
S3: VC script rehearsal — student reads aloud, teacher provides pronunciation feedback.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: Pull-out oral tasks (teacher does these with 1–2 students while class works):
S1 pull-out: Show flashcard of base verb ("make") → student says past form ("made"), meaning, and 1 sentence ("I made my bed").
S2 pull-out: Prompt a scenario ("Your room was a mess"). Student answers using key verbs ("I did my chores and made my bed").
S3 pull-out: Assess VC script fluency. Check for overgeneralization errors like "maked" or "taked".

Communicative task (Step 5 — 10 min — MUST have real information gap): Students work in pairs to discover a character's busy schedule. Materials needed: Print 2 copies of Card A and 2 copies of Card B per pair (Section 8). Step-by-step:
Give Card A to Student A, Card B to Student B. Ensure they hide their cards.
Students ask provided questions to complete the missing tasks.
Students produce: A fully ordered daily schedule using sequence words and task verbs.
did: Cross arms and nod firmly (task completed).
made: Mime shaping something with hands.
took (a photo/shower): Mime clicking a camera OR scrubbing hair under water.
mess: Wiggle fingers randomly in the air to show chaos.
